dimension.category_description: How multiple possibilities are presented, previewed, maintained, blended, or compared before commitment.
dimension.classification_boundary: Requires a visible choice or comparison mechanism, not backend candidate-set processing alone.

candidates.title: DataDive: Supporting Readers' Contextualization of Statistical Statements with Data Exploration
candidates.why: DataDive generates multiple contextual questions for one statistical statement, presents them as alternatives, and lets the user select one to initiate the corresponding visualization and data exploration. The evidence captures the candidate fork, visible choice, single selection, and downstream commitment with unusual completeness.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over AnnotateGPT because its candidate selection is equally explicit but demonstrates the pattern in a richer, broadly transferable sensemaking task rather than an intent-routing step.
candidates.pattern_summary: At a single decision point the system emits more than one alternative for the same request and presents them together as a set.
candidates.structural_signature: Control flow forks at one point into N ≥ 2 outputs of the same type, all rendered simultaneously in a bounded display region (a row, a side-by-side triple, a separate list beside the working surface). A selection event on one member is the commit action: it writes that member into the downstream state and terminates the other branches. The multiplicity is in the outputs, not in the operations offered over one output, and the set is resolved in a single act.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus order by excluding rid 5922, despite its second-place mean, and promoting rid 6169 into the final three. The 5922 evidence establishes selection among generated options but does not establish that they are rendered simultaneously, and its iterative optimization loop weakens the pattern's single-decision-point and single-act resolution requirements; its high rater spread reflects this ambiguity. No selected score was adjusted by more than 0.3. Readers should still treat the exact visual layout as unverified for all three: the excerpts establish presented alternatives and selection, but only rid 7136 explicitly states a fixed set of three answers, while none explicitly documents how rejected branches are visually discarded or backgrounded. Rid 7136 also leaves the downstream state change more implicit than rid 10160 and rid 6169.

candidates.title: VideoDiff: Human-AI Video Co-Creation with Alternatives
candidates.why: The strongest structural match: comparable videos are explicitly aligned and shown together, with differences exposed across synchronized timelines, transcripts, and previews. It demonstrates both the canonical parallel layout and an unusually rich diff encoding for time-based, multimodal artifacts.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over rid 10955 because its evidence establishes alignment and corresponding-part comparison across multiple representations, not merely the availability of a juxtaposed view.
candidates.pattern_summary: Two or more instances of the same kind of artifact are displayed simultaneously in parallel regions so that their differences can be read off directly.
candidates.structural_signature: Two or more renderings of comparable objects occupy spatially parallel regions at the same time, with corresponding parts aligned across regions. The comparison quantity is the visual difference between regions, and the display may add a diff encoding over the alignment. Slot assignment is a user action ("select any two…") or a fixed before/after pairing.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus top three by selecting rid 12304 instead of rid 16920. The adjustment is small: 12304 rises from 4.25 to 4.35 because its quote independently establishes nearly the entire structural signature, while 16920's evidence confirms a side-by-side mode but supplies little detail about simultaneous alignment. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should still be cautious: the evidence for rid 4474 comes only from an abstract, rid 10955 from a figure caption with a typographical error ('juxtapositon'), and rid 12304 from a short system-section excerpt; none of the supplied evidence establishes measured user outcomes. I also avoided selecting both LLM Comparator records, which share the same underlying system concept despite having different supplied system_id values.

candidates.title: Spellburst: A Node-based Interface for Exploratory Creative Coding with Natural Language Prompts
candidates.why: Spellburst makes persistent alternatives the interface itself: artists create variation branches in a node graph and can merge paths without destroying their separate histories.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It outranks Branchat because it supports both forking and recombination in a visible node graph, demonstrating a richer form of branching exploration than conversation-tree navigation alone.
candidates.pattern_summary: The interaction is organized as a tree or open graph in which alternatives coexist, rather than as a single ordered track the user advances along.
candidates.structural_signature: State is held as multiple simultaneously extant paths from a shared origin; a control exists for creating a new path and for switching which path is active; paths are displayed together (as a tree, a canvas of branches, or parallel panels) so their coexistence is visible. Advancing along one path does not destroy the others.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by moving rid 10375 (-generAItor) out of the final three and elevating rids 9118 and 13801. The visible beam-search tree in -generAItor is compelling, but the supplied evidence emphasizes inspecting, explaining, and adapting a model-generated tree rather than explicitly creating and switching among user-controlled branches, leaving part of the structural signature unverified. I raised Branchat by 0.15 and ImaginationVellum by 0.05 because their evidence more directly establishes nondestructive forking from retained prior states; no adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should still be cautious that the short excerpts do not independently document every required control: Spellburst's abstract does not explicitly describe active-path switching, Branchat's excerpt does not state that all branches are simultaneously displayed, and ImaginationVellum's excerpt leaves canvas navigation mechanics implicit.

candidates.title: DSCode Comparator: An Interactive Interface for Comparing Models and Evaluating Code for Data Science Tasks
candidates.why: The evidence directly establishes one shared prompt—and optionally one shared dataset—being dispatched to multiple LLMs, while the system’s explicit purpose supplies the common comparison frame for their code outputs.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over MoWa because multiple-model invocation and output comparison are both central and explicit, whereas MoWa’s evidence establishes the fan-out more clearly than the comparative presentation.
candidates.pattern_summary: A single user request is dispatched unchanged to several distinct models at once, and their outputs are returned together.
candidates.structural_signature: Fan-out control flow: one input, n parallel invocations differing only in which backend is called, n outputs collected and presented in a common frame with source attribution. The key structural fact is that the *generator* is the varied dimension while the input is held constant — the inverse of perturbation probing. Transplants to any plural-backend setting: several solvers, several translation engines, several search indices.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by moving rid 4519 above rid 2325: MoWa’s evidence more directly proves the defining held-input, varied-generator structure, while ChainForge’s quote combines model comparison with prompt variation. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3. Readers should distrust any stronger claim that these excerpts prove simultaneous execution or explicit source labels: none does. DSCode Comparator and MoWa also lack direct quoted evidence of the exact common-frame layout, while ChainForge does not explicitly establish that an unchanged prompt is sent to every model.

candidates.title: From Text to Pixels: Enhancing User Understanding through Text-to-Image Model Explanations
candidates.why: The system performs the complete perturb-and-compare loop: it applies a known keyword-removal transformation to an existing prompt, regenerates the image, and evaluates the altered result against the original, making the induced difference legible.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over rid 12842 because its evidence explicitly covers both controlled input alteration and comparison with the original output, whereas rid 12842’s quote establishes the perturbation controls but not the rerun or comparative display.
candidates.pattern_summary: The interface takes an input the model has already been run on, applies a controlled alteration to it, re-runs the model, and presents the altered-input output against the original one.
candidates.structural_signature: Control flow: for a held input x, the system constructs one or more variants x' by a user-specified transformation rule (granularity, target, magnitude), executes the same model on x and each x', and joins the outputs into a paired or batched display keyed to the transformation that produced each. The distinguishing structure is that the delta is *induced by the interface* rather than found in the data, so the manipulated dimension is known to the system and can be used as the organizing axis of the display. This transplants: the same signature describes a spreadsheet what-if sweep, a compiler flag sweep, or an injected-decoy audit of a retrieval index.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final selection retains the consensus top three, but scores rid 12842 and rid 2325 slightly below their consensus means because their quoted evidence does not explicitly show the model rerun and joined original-versus-altered output display required by the full structural signature. Rid 10126 has the strongest structural evidence, though even its quote leaves user authorship or parameterization of the redaction somewhat implicit. Readers should therefore treat only rid 10126 as a fully evidenced instance from the supplied quotations; the other two are strong exemplars whose complete comparison loops depend partly on their stated system contexts and titles.

candidates.title: Investigating Semantically-enhanced Exploration of GAN Latent Space via a Digital Mood Board
candidates.why: The interaction nearly reproduces the structural signature step by step: the user separately selects two existing groups, invokes a named Mix operation for each, and receives a synthesized style mixture between the identifiable operands.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen above VoiceForge because its evidence explicitly distinguishes operand selection from operator invocation and documents the complete interaction sequence.
candidates.pattern_summary: The user selects two or more existing items and invokes an operation whose product is a single fused result rather than either operand.
candidates.structural_signature: An operator takes two or more selected items as arguments and returns a result in the same space as the arguments; where the mixing is continuous, a control exposes the position between operands. Selecting the operands and invoking the operator are separate acts, and the result can itself become an operand.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained the consensus top three but reversed the first two: rid 7000 ranks first because its quote most explicitly proves the signature's separate selection and invocation acts. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The main evidentiary weakness is that none of the three quotes confirms that a fused result can itself become a later operand. VoiceForge also leaves the generated same-space result implicit, while DanceGen does not document its blend control or output presentation.
